# Remote Code

[中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Use OpenCode to work on a remote machine over SSH. The plugin redirects `shell`,
`glob`, `grep`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, and `patch` to the remote target. Commands
run over SSH; file tools use SFTP. No remote agent installation is required.

**Install once in your global OpenCode config, then use `/remote connect` to switch
the current session to SSH.** Other sessions stay local; `/remote disconnect`
switches the session back to local tools.

## Requirements

- OpenCode 2.2.7+ (V2 instruction-source metadata is required), compatible with the `@opencode/plugin` version in [package.json](package.json).
- Node.js 20+ for the plugin's Node runtime and tests.
- A remote SSH server with SFTP and a POSIX shell, or OpenSSH for Windows with
  PowerShell 5.1/7. No remote Node.js, Python, Git, or ripgrep is needed.

## Quick start: install globally, connect per session

### 1. Build the plugin

The scoped npm package is not published yet. Build a local checkout using the pnpm
version pinned in `package.json`:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hzrd149/opencode-remote-code.git
cd opencode-remote-code
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
```

### 2. Enable it globally

Add this entry to `plugins` in **`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`** (or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.jsonc` when set). Use the absolute path to your
built checkout and keep your other configuration entries:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-remote-code",
      "options": { "runtime": true }
    }
  ]
}
```

This makes `/remote` available across projects. Sessions start with local tools;
no SSH connection is opened until you connect. Leave `ssh`, `host`, and `activateIn`
out of this global runtime configuration. OpenCode reloads configuration changes
automatically; use `/reload` if needed.

### 3. Switch the current session to SSH

Open OpenCode in your usual project directory, or use an existing session. Enter:

```text
/remote connect server.example
/remote status
```

Once connected, file and shell tools in **this session** operate on the remote
machine. The username defaults to your local OS user (on the OpenCode service
host), and the working directory defaults to the remote login home, resolved
over SFTP. Other sessions are unaffected. To select a user and project explicitly:

```text
/remote disconnect
/remote connect alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

To return to local tools:

```text
/remote disconnect
```

To change SSH targets, disconnect first, then run `/remote connect` with the new
target. For a Windows target, use a path such as `C:/Users/alice/project`.
Omit `--key` to use an SSH agent available to the OpenCode service, or supply
`--agent-socket` explicitly. Passwords must use the runtime RPC, not command text.
See [connection arguments](docs/usage.md#connection-arguments) for all supported flags.

Once published, `@hzrd149/opencode-remote-code` can replace the local `package`
path in the same global configuration; keep `"options": { "runtime": true }`.

## Important behavior

### Connect from the terminal

With the global runtime configuration above, you can also connect before opening
the OpenCode UI:

```sh
node /absolute/path/to/opencode-remote-code/dist/cli-main.js alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project
```

The installed executable is `remote-opencode`. It captures the terminal's
`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, creates a stable local session directory, connects through typed
RPC, and attaches to that session. No model call is needed to connect.
In-session controls are `/remote status`, `/remote disconnect`, and
`/remote connect alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project`.
Host-only connections such as `/remote connect server.example` or
`/remote connect 192.168.1.20` default to your local OS username and the remote
login home (resolved over SFTP). Quote paths with spaces:
`/remote connect alice@host --workdir '/path with spaces'`.
Use `--port 2222`, `--user alice`, `--agent-socket /path/to/agent`, or `--key /path/to/key`
as needed. The CLI accepts the same target options (`--agent-socket` overrides its
calling terminal's `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`); the slash command uses the service's configured
authentication unless explicitly overridden. IPv6 may be bare or bracketed
(`alice@[::1]`); specify ports separately with `--port`, never `host:port`.
Arguments support quotes and backslash escapes, with no shell evaluation or
variable expansion. `/remote connect --help` shows usage. The previous JSON target
form remains supported; passwords must use RPC rather than slash-command text.
Connections are session-specific; interrupted or failed remote sessions block
file/shell tools until reconnect or explicit disconnect. Passwords use RPC,
not slash-command text. Remote subagent delegation is disabled.

- **Runtime mode switches one session at a time.** For a fixed target instead,
  omit `runtime` and configure `ssh`/`host` in plugin options. In that mode,
  `activateIn` restricts activation to matching local session directories;
  without it, the configured target is active everywhere. See [configuration](docs/configuration.md).
- `workdir` is a **remote** path. It defaults to the SSH user's home; relative
  paths and `~` resolve there. Windows absolute paths need a drive letter, such
  as `C:/Users/me/project`.
- Authentication uses `key`, `password`, or a local SSH agent (`agentSocket`,
  otherwise the service's `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`), in that order. Agent forwarding is disabled.
  The `ssh` string is parsed, not
  executed, and does not provide full OpenSSH command-line behavior.
- Remote files are mirrored locally as needed. There is no remote LSP, and
  SFTP searches can be slower than running ripgrep on the server.
- Runtime sessions have isolated mirrors; fixed-target sessions share them.
  Avoid concurrent edits to the same remote files. Currently,
  `patch` delete hunks empty files rather than remove them; use `shell` to delete.

## Documentation

### Remote instructions

OpenCode's model prompts, custom agents, skills, Code Mode, MCP guidance and session
instruction entries are preserved. The plugin replaces `core/environment` with remote
OS/shell/workspace details and `core/instructions` with the remote root `AGENTS.md`,
read once at setup. This replaces the entire discovered-file source, including local
global/configured instruction files; use custom agent instructions for shared policies.
Nested remote instruction discovery is not automatic. Generate/compaction requests
receive the same edits when they contain these sources; title prompts are untouched.
Stored history is unchanged, so old local instruction updates can remain in the transcript;
the remote context explicitly distinguishes them. No model prompt templates are bundled.

- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): options, SSH syntax, paths, search limits.
- [Usage and troubleshooting](docs/usage.md): launchers, installation, tool behavior,
  and limitations.
- [Test harness](test/README.md): test commands, coverage, and platform requirements.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): changes since the fork and release notes for npm.

## Development

Use `nvm use` for the default development Node version and the pnpm version in
`package.json`. From the repository root:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
pnpm run lint
MOCK_SSH_BASH=/bin/bash pnpm test --dialect=posix
```

Tests use Node + `tsx`; Windows integration tests need Windows and PowerShell.
See the [test guide](test/README.md) for platform requirements and runner options.

Run `pnpm dev` to build the plugin and open an interactive OpenCode session with
the local build and runtime connections enabled. OpenCode must be on `PATH`.
The launcher uses a private server (`--standalone`) and an ignored local session
directory at `tmp_test_artifacts/dev`; your usual providers and credentials remain
available. Inside the session, connect to a remote:

```text
/remote connect alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project
```

Use your terminal's SSH agent, or add `--key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to the connection
arguments. Check `/remote status` to confirm the connection. Development launcher
arguments match the `remote-opencode` CLI and connect before opening the TUI:

```sh
pnpm dev alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project --port 2222 --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
pnpm dev --help
```

All CLI options, including `--user` and `--session`, are supported. Target-specific
development sessions live beneath `tmp_test_artifacts/dev` and use a private
server that stops when the TUI exits. Use a development session ID with `--session`.
After source changes, exit and rerun `pnpm dev` to load a fresh build.
`pnpm dev:watch` runs only the TypeScript compiler in watch mode.

# Remote Code

[English](README.md)

通过 SSH 使用 OpenCode 操作远程机器。插件将 `shell`、`glob`、`grep`、
`read`、`write`、`edit` 和 `patch` 指向远端：命令通过 SSH 执行，文件工具
通过 SFTP 操作。远端无需安装 Agent。

**在 OpenCode 全局配置中安装一次，即可用 `/remote connect` 将当前会话切换到 SSH。**
其他会话仍使用本地工具；用 `/remote disconnect` 切回本地。

## 环境要求

- OpenCode 2.2.7+（需要 V2 指令来源元数据），兼容 [package.json](package.json) 中的 `@opencode/plugin` 版本。
- 插件的 Node 运行环境及测试需要 Node.js 20+。
- 远端提供 SSH、SFTP 和 POSIX shell；Windows 远端需 OpenSSH for Windows
  和 PowerShell 5.1/7。远端无需 Node.js、Python、Git 或 ripgrep。

## 快速开始：全局安装，按会话连接

### 1. 构建插件

该 scoped npm 包尚未发布。使用 `package.json` 固定的 pnpm 版本构建本地源码：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hzrd149/opencode-remote-code.git
cd opencode-remote-code
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
```

### 2. 全局启用

在 **`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`** 中的 `plugins` 添加以下条目
（设置了 `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` 时使用 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.jsonc`）。
将路径替换为已构建源码的绝对路径，并保留其他配置：

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-remote-code",
      "options": { "runtime": true }
    }
  ]
}
```

这样即可在各个项目中使用 `/remote`。会话初始使用本地工具，连接前不会建立 SSH。
此全局运行时配置不要设置 `ssh`、`host` 或 `activateIn`。
OpenCode 会自动重新加载配置，必要时使用 `/reload`。

### 3. 将当前会话切换到 SSH

在通常的项目目录打开 OpenCode，或使用已有会话，输入：

```text
/remote connect server.example
/remote status
```

连接后，**当前会话**的文件和 shell 工具在远端执行。用户名默认为运行 OpenCode
服务的本地操作系统用户，工作目录默认为通过 SFTP 获取的远端登录主目录。
其他会话不受影响。若需指定用户、项目和私钥，先断开再连接：

```text
/remote disconnect
/remote connect alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

在同一会话继续聊天即可操作远端。切回本地：

```text
/remote disconnect
```

更换目标时先断开，再执行新的 `/remote connect`。Windows 工作目录可以使用
`C:/Users/alice/project`。省略 `--key` 时使用 OpenCode 服务可访问的 SSH agent，
也可通过 `--agent-socket /path/to/agent` 显式指定。两者不能同时使用。
`--user alice` 可指定用户名，`--port 2222` 可指定端口（默认 22）。
含空格的路径需加引号，例如 `--workdir 'C:/My Project'`。
IPv6 可使用 `alice@[::1]`；端口必须单独用 `--port`，不支持 `host:port`。
参数支持引号和反斜杠转义，不执行 shell 或变量展开；Windows 路径建议使用正斜杠。
`/remote connect --help` 显示帮助。密码只能通过运行时 RPC 传递，不能放入命令文本。
发布后可将 `package` 路径替换为 `@hzrd149/opencode-remote-code`，保留
`"options": { "runtime": true }`。

## 重要行为

- 终端也可运行 `node /absolute/path/to/opencode-remote-code/dist/cli-main.js server.example`。
  安装后的命令名为 `remote-opencode`，使用相同的连接参数，并支持 `--session ID`。
  CLI 捕获调用终端的 `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`（可用 `--agent-socket` 覆盖），创建稳定的本地
  会话目录，通过 RPC 连接后打开界面；无需模型调用。详细参数见[使用指南](docs/usage.md#connection-arguments)。
- 连接中断、失败或服务重启后，远程会话的文件与 shell 工具会阻止执行，直到重新连接
  或显式断开；不会静默切回本地。远程会话禁用子 agent 委派。
- **运行时模式按会话切换。** 若需固定目标，可省略 `runtime` 并在插件选项中配置
  `ssh`/`host`。该模式的 `activateIn` 匹配本地会话目录；省略时固定目标在所有目录生效。
- `workdir` 是**远程**路径，默认是 SSH 用户的主目录；相对路径和 `~` 均
  相对于该目录解析。Windows 绝对路径必须带盘符，例如 `C:/Users/me/project`。
- 认证优先级为 `key`、`password`、本地 SSH agent（`agentSocket` 或服务的
  `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`），不启用 agent 转发。`ssh` 字符串仅被解析，不会直接执行，
  也不支持完整的 OpenSSH 命令行行为。
- 文件按需镜像到本地。不支持远程 LSP；SFTP 搜索可能比服务器上的 ripgrep 慢。
- 运行时会话的镜像相互隔离，固定目标会话共享镜像；避免同时编辑同一远端文件。
  目前 `patch` 的删除块会
  清空文件而非删除文件；需要删除时使用 `shell`。

## 文档

### 远程指令

保留 OpenCode 模型提示词、自定义 agent、skills、Code Mode、MCP 和会话指令。
仅替换 `core/environment` 和 `core/instructions`：后者整体替换为启动时读取的
远程根目录 `AGENTS.md`，包括替换本地全局及配置的指令文件。通用规则可放入自定义
agent 指令。不会自动发现远程子目录指令。generate/compaction 请求含有这些来源时
也会更新，title 请求不受影响。历史记录不变，可能仍包含旧的本地指令更新；远程
上下文会明确区分。不再内置模型提示词模板。

以下参考文档使用英文维护：

- [配置参考](docs/configuration.md)：选项、SSH 语法、路径和搜索限制。
- [使用与故障排查](docs/usage.md)：启动器、安装、工具行为及限制。
- [测试指南](test/README.md)：测试命令、覆盖范围和平台要求。

## 开发

通过 `nvm use` 选择默认开发 Node 版本，使用 `package.json` 固定的 pnpm 版本。
在仓库根目录运行：

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
pnpm run lint
MOCK_SSH_BASH=/bin/bash pnpm test --dialect=posix
```

测试通过 Node + `tsx` 运行；Windows 集成测试需要 Windows 和 PowerShell。
平台要求与运行选项见[测试指南](test/README.md)。

# Changelog

Notable changes to `@hzrd149/opencode-remote-code` since the personal fork of
[vibed-this/opencode-remote-code](https://github.com/vibed-this/opencode-remote-code).
The fork starts after upstream commit
[`1c28420`](https://github.com/hzrd149/opencode-remote-code/commit/1c28420)
(version 3.0.1). Earlier features, including the OpenCode V2 port, Windows support,
and `activateIn`, belong to upstream history.

## Unreleased

These entries cover the first scoped npm release, including current working-tree
changes. The inherited `package.json` version is not a published fork release.
When publishing, replace this heading with the release version and date, and
start a new `Unreleased` section for subsequent changes.

### Added

- Optional per-session SSH connections with `runtime: true` and `/remote connect`,
  `/remote status`, and `/remote disconnect`. Install globally while keeping other
  sessions local.
- Typed runtime RPC, exported through the package's `/rpc` entry point, for
  programmatic connection management and credentials outside command text.
- Session-isolated runtime mirrors and routing. Failed or restored remote
  sessions block local tool fallback until reconnect or explicit disconnect;
  stale tool calls are rejected after target changes.
- The `remote-opencode` CLI to create or attach to local OpenCode sessions backed
  by SSH, using stable local session directories and the caller's SSH agent.
- Local SSH-agent authentication through `agentSocket` or `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, with
  explicit keys and passwords taking precedence. Agent forwarding stays disabled.
- A `pnpm dev` launcher for the local plugin build with a private OpenCode server,
  interactive connection setup, and CLI-compatible target arguments.

### Changed

- Prepare publication as the public scoped package `@hzrd149/opencode-remote-code`,
  with fork-specific repository, issue tracker, and package links.
- Preserve OpenCode's native model prompts, custom agents, skills, Code Mode,
  MCP guidance, and session instructions. Replace only the keyed environment and
  discovered-file instruction sources with remote context and root `AGENTS.md`.
- Require OpenCode 2.2.7+ for instruction-source metadata and align the plugin and
  client dependencies with that API.
- Migrate development and test tooling to pnpm and TypeScript with `tsx`; default
  development to Node.js 26 while retaining Node.js 20+ support.
- Streamline the English and Chinese READMEs, move configuration and usage
  references into `docs/`, and document global setup and per-session connections.
- Limit npm contents to release assets and rebuild before packing. Include this
  changelog in the published package.

### Fixed

- Avoid replacing OpenCode's complete prompt with bundled templates, including
  during generation and compaction; leave title prompts and stored history intact.
- Correct runtime tool-result compatibility with OpenCode: content-only file
  tools no longer inherit native output codecs, and shell results provide the
  structured completion output and metadata expected by the host.
- Make the test harness portable across local hosts, including platform-aware
  paths, shell selection, and Windows integration-test requirements.

### Removed

- Bundled model prompt templates and their build-time copying step.
- Historical migration and design documents superseded by the maintained READMEs
  and implementation comments.

### Tests

- Add coverage for SSH-agent authentication, runtime routing and isolation,
  targeted instruction replacement, and CLI parsing and attachment.
- Add opt-in real OpenCode host tests for runtime and CLI connections, including
  a local fake model exercising remote tools through the host's tool pipeline.

# Configuration

[README](../README.md) · [Usage and troubleshooting](usage.md)

Configure the remote through `plugins[].options` in `opencode.jsonc`. Without
`ssh` or `host`, the plugin stays dormant unless `runtime: true` is set. Runtime
mode exposes per-session connection RPC and `/remote` commands; do not configure
a static `ssh`/`host` alongside it. Invalid target configuration is
reported and leaves OpenCode running without the remote tools.

## Options

For per-session connections, set `runtime: true` and use `/remote connect host`.
The username defaults to the local OS user on the service host; the remote workdir
defaults to the SFTP login home. See [connection arguments](usage.md#connection-arguments)
for slash-command and CLI flags. The `ssh` option syntax below applies to fixed
configuration and RPC targets, not to the shell-style `/remote connect` command.

Use these canonical names. Compatibility aliases are listed in
[`OPTION_KEYS`](../src/config.ts).

| Option | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime` | `false` | Enable per-session `/remote` commands and RPC; do not combine with static `ssh`/`host` |
| `ssh` | — | Parsed SSH command string; alternative to `host` |
| `host` | — | Remote hostname or IP |
| `port` | `22` | SSH port |
| `user` | Local OS username | Remote username |
| `key` | — | Local private-key file; expands `~` |
| `password` | — | Password authentication; a configured key takes precedence |
| `agentSocket` | Service `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` | Local SSH-agent socket when no key/password is configured; never forwarded |
| `workdir` | Remote login home | Default remote working directory |
| `platform` | `"auto"` | `"auto"`, `"posix"`, or `"windows"` |
| `shell` | Auto-selected | `bash` on POSIX; `pwsh.exe` if found, otherwise `powershell.exe` on Windows |
| `activateIn` | `[]` (everywhere) | Local directory or array of directories in which to activate |
| `mirror` | `~/.opencode/mirrors` | Local mirror root |
| `debug` | `false` | Append diagnostics to `~/.opencode/remote-code-debug.log` |
| `ignore` | `[]` | Extra directory names to exclude from traversal |
| `limits` | See below | Search, traversal, and shell budgets |
| `timeout` | `120000` ms | Default shell timeout; overrides `limits.shellTimeout` |
| `pool` | `{ "command": 3, "file": 4, "stagger": 0 }` | Command/file connection counts and handshake stagger in milliseconds |

### Activation scope

`activateIn` refers to **local session directories**, not remote paths. It
accepts a string or array, expands `~`, and includes descendants of each directory.
Matching respects directory boundaries and is case-insensitive on Windows hosts.

```jsonc
"activateIn": ["~/.opencode/remote-sessions", "/home/me/remote-work"]
```

Outside the scope, or when the session directory is unavailable, the plugin is
dormant. An absent or empty scope activates it everywhere a target is configured.
Active sessions replace all seven native tools; they do not get a second set of
local file tools.

## SSH connection

Prefer explicit connection and authentication settings:

```jsonc
"options": {
  "host": "192.0.2.10",
  "port": 2222,
  "user": "me",
  "key": "~/.ssh/id_ed25519",
  "workdir": "/home/me/project"
}
```

Alternatively, set `ssh` to `"ssh -p 2222 -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 me@192.0.2.10"`.
The string is parsed by the plugin; connections use `ssh2`, not a local `ssh`
process. Conflicting host, port, user, or identity values between the two forms
are rejected.

| Syntax | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `user@host`, `host`, `user@[::1]` | Target |
| `-p 2222`, `-p2222`, `--port=2222` | Port |
| `-i <path>`, `--identity <path>` | Identity file |
| `-l user`, `-luser` | Username |
| `ssh://user@host:2222` | URL form; embedded passwords are rejected |
| Single/double quotes | Paths containing spaces; unquoted backslashes remain literal |

An optional `ssh` executable name/path is discarded. `ssh_config` is not read;
`-F` does not load it. Use explicit hosts and credentials rather than relying on
SSH aliases. Authentication precedence is key, password, then SSH agent. Set
`agentSocket` explicitly when the calling terminal's agent differs from the
background service environment. The plugin never loads keys into the agent.

The parser accepts `-o` keys `StrictHostKeyChecking`, `UserKnownHostsFile`,
`ConnectTimeout`, `ServerAliveInterval`, `ServerAliveCountMax`, `HostKeyAlgorithms`,
and `IdentitiesOnly`. **Acceptance does not imply OpenSSH-equivalent behavior:**
the current connection pool applies host-key algorithms and the explicit
`StrictHostKeyChecking=no` setting, but does not implement known-hosts verification
or wire the other accepted settings into its connection configuration. Unknown
`-o` keys produce a warning and are ignored.

Jump hosts/proxy commands (`-J`, `ProxyJump`, `ProxyCommand`), forwarding
(`-L`, `-R`, `-D`), and PTY requests (`-t`, `RequestTTY`) are rejected. For a
jump host, establish a tunnel separately and connect the plugin to its local port:

```sh
ssh -N -L 2222:target-host:22 jump-user@jump-host
```

Then use `host: "127.0.0.1"` and `port: 2222`. Operations run with the SSH user's
permissions; the removed `sudoPassword` option does not enable privilege escalation.

## Platforms and paths

The plugin detects the remote platform from SFTP's login-home path. Set
`platform` explicitly if a chroot or unusual SFTP server makes detection ambiguous.

| `workdir` | POSIX | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omitted | Login home | Login home |
| `proj`, `src/app`, `~`, `~/proj` | Relative to login home | Relative to login home |
| `/home/me/project` | Absolute path | Rejected: no drive letter |
| `C:/Users/me/project` | Not a POSIX absolute path | Absolute path |
| `C:project` | Not a POSIX absolute path | Rejected: drive-relative path |

Use forward slashes in JSON Windows paths to avoid escaping backslashes.
PowerShell is selected automatically on Windows; POSIX defaults to `bash`.

## Search limits and ignores

Set individual values inside `limits`; unspecified values retain their defaults.
Values must be positive numbers (numeric strings are also accepted).

| Key | Default | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globResults` | `100` | Glob results |
| `searchMatches` | `100` | Grep matches |
| `searchBytes` | `67108864` (64 MiB) | Total bytes searched |
| `searchFileSize` | `2097152` (2 MiB) | Largest file searched |
| `searchMillis` | `45000` | Search/traversal time in milliseconds |
| `walkDepth` | `12` | Traversal depth |
| `walkEntries` | `20000` | Directory entries visited |
| `shellTimeout` | `120000` | Shell timeout in milliseconds |

`ignore` **extends** the built-in directory-name exclusions; it does not replace
them or accept gitignore rules. Names match at any depth, case-insensitively only
on Windows remotes. Defaults:

```text
node_modules .git .hg .svn dist build out target .venv venv vendor
__pycache__ .next .cache .turbo $RECYCLE.BIN System Volume Information
Windows.old .pnpm-store .Trash
```

Results include truncation notices when budgets are reached. Narrow the search
root/pattern before raising limits on large remote trees.

# Usage and troubleshooting

[README](../README.md) · [Configuration](configuration.md)

## Per-session connections

Enable `"options": { "runtime": true }` in the global plugin entry as shown in
the [README](../README.md). In any session:

```text
/remote connect server.example
/remote status
/remote disconnect
/remote connect alice@server.example --port 2222 --workdir '/srv/my project'
```

Only the current session switches to remote tools. Disconnect before changing
targets. Failed or restored remote sessions block file/shell tools until you
reconnect or explicitly disconnect. Remote subagent delegation is disabled.

### Connection arguments

`/remote connect [user@]host [options]` and `remote-opencode [user@]host [options]`
accept these flags, each followed by a separate value:

| Flag | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `--user USER` | Local OS username; may instead be included in `user@host` |
| `--workdir PATH` | Remote login home, resolved through SFTP; relative paths resolve there |
| `--port PORT` | `22`; integer from 1 to 65535 |
| `--key PATH` | Local private key; `~` expands locally |
| `--agent-socket PATH` | Explicit local SSH-agent socket; cannot be combined with `--key` |
| `--help`, `-h` | Show usage, without connecting |
| `--session ID` | CLI only: reconnect an existing session belonging to the same target directory |

Without an explicit authentication flag, the slash command uses configured service
authentication (key, password, then agent). The CLI uses the calling terminal's
`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`; `--agent-socket` overrides it. If neither an agent nor a key is
available, the CLI fails before opening the UI. Passwords are accepted through
runtime RPC, not slash-command text or CLI flags.

Use a hostname, IPv4, or IPv6 address (`::1` or `alice@[::1]`). Specify ports with
`--port`, never `host:port`. SSH config aliases, URLs and full `ssh` commands are
not accepted here. Repeated flags and conflicting usernames are rejected.
The slash command supports single/double quotes and backslash escapes, without
shell evaluation or variable expansion. Prefer forward slashes for Windows paths,
for example `--workdir 'C:/My Project'`. In terminal commands, your shell processes
quoting before the CLI receives arguments. Legacy JSON slash-command targets
remain supported.

## Stable sessions and launchers

OpenCode associates sessions with the local working directory. Reuse the same
local directory to return to a remote project's sessions.

The runtime CLI connects before opening the UI:

```sh
node /absolute/path/to/opencode-remote-code/dist/cli-main.js server.example
# Installed executable:
remote-opencode alice@server.example --workdir /srv/project
```

It creates a stable directory under `~/.opencode/remote-sessions/` from the host,
port, user and workdir, then creates a session and connects through typed RPC.
Use `--session ID` to reconnect a disconnected session in that directory. Closing
the UI does not disconnect; `/remote disconnect` explicitly returns to local tools.

The older optional scripts in `launchers/` choose a stable directory under
`~/.opencode/remote-sessions/`, derived from the host and remote workdir:

```sh
bash launchers/remote-opencode.sh --ssh "ssh me@192.0.2.10" --workdir /home/me/project
```

On Windows, use the PowerShell launcher (a `.bat` wrapper is also provided):

```powershell
.\launchers\remote-opencode.ps1 --ssh "ssh me@192.0.2.10" --workdir C:/Users/me/project
```

These arguments **only name the local session directory**. Configure the actual
connection in `opencode.jsonc`; keep the launcher values consistent with it.
Pair launchers with `activateIn: "~/.opencode/remote-sessions"` to keep other
local projects using native tools. Other arguments are forwarded to OpenCode;
`--` explicitly separates forwarded arguments. Legacy `REMOTE_SSH` and
`REMOTE_WORKDIR` environment variables also supply directory-naming values.

## Local installation troubleshooting

If the plugin appears inactive:

1. Build the checkout and use its **absolute path** in `plugins[].package`.
   Keep the root `index.js` shim alongside `dist/`; local discovery uses it.
2. Use an object entry with `package` and `options`. Auto-discovery alone does
   not supply connection options, so the plugin remains dormant.
3. In runtime mode, ensure `runtime: true` is set and run `/remote connect host`.
   For fixed targets, check `activateIn` against the **local** session directory,
   and ensure `ssh` or `host` is configured.
4. Use `/reload` if needed and open a real session. A config
   inspection command alone does not establish that the plugin has loaded.
5. Enable `options.debug` and inspect `~/.opencode/remote-code-debug.log`.

For a stable local install, keep a built checkout near your OpenCode configuration
and reference it explicitly. Avoid also placing it in an auto-discovered plugins
directory, which can result in duplicate loading. If a Windows installation on
another drive fails discovery, try a checkout on the same drive as the config;
cross-drive behavior can depend on the OpenCode version.

## Tool behavior

Only `shell` executes remote commands. All other tools use SFTP; reads and edits
mirror individual files locally rather than copying a whole project.

| Tool | Details worth knowing |
| --- | --- |
| `shell` | Uses the remote shell and workspace by default; reports timeouts separately from nonzero exit codes. No interactive PTY. |
| `glob` | Supports `*`, `?`, `**`, braces, and character classes. Patterns without `/` match basenames; results are newest-first. |
| `grep` | Uses JavaScript regular expressions, not ripgrep's regex engine. Leading `(?i)`, `(?m)`, and `(?s)` flags are accepted; `include` is a glob. |
| `read` | Lists directories or reads text; rejects binary files. Default output is bounded to 2,000 lines and 50 KB. |
| `write`, `edit` | Preserve existing line endings and BOMs; edits use per-file locks and permission previews. |
| `patch` | Accepts native patch format and unified diffs. Moves rename remotely; delete hunks currently empty the file. |

Search limits and ignored directories are configurable in the
[configuration reference](configuration.md#search-limits-and-ignores).

## Limitations

- **No remote LSP:** remote file tools do not supply language-server diagnostics.
- **Transfer/search cost:** first access transfers the file over SFTP; searching
  large trees can be slower than native server-side tools. Use narrow paths.
- **Concurrent sessions:** runtime sessions have isolated mirrors. Fixed-target
  sessions for the same SSH identity/host/port share a mirror namespace, cleared
  at startup. Locks are per-session; concurrent edits to the same remote file
  can still overwrite each other.
- **Patch deletion:** delete hunks empty files instead of unlinking them. Use
  `shell` for actual deletion.
- **Windows output:** mixed UTF-8 and CP936/GBK in one stream may decode poorly.
  UNC paths are best-effort and have not been verified against a real SMB-backed
  OpenSSH server.
- **Server compatibility:** shell results rely on SSH channel exit codes. Older
  servers need validation; no server-version check enforces an OpenSSH 8 floor.
  The current algorithm list includes `ssh-rsa`, contrary to older documentation.

## Local data and remote permissions

Mirrored files live under `~/.opencode/mirrors` unless configured otherwise.
Treat those copies as local copies of the remote data. Mirror containment checks
prevent mapped paths from escaping their namespace; paths outside the remote
workspace go through OpenCode's permission system.

Commands and file operations use the SSH account's permissions. No remote agent
is installed, but commands can change remote state; oversized PowerShell scripts
are temporarily staged over SFTP and removed afterward. Debug logging omits
passwords and private-key paths. See the [SSH reference](configuration.md#ssh-connection)
for the current host-verification and option-handling limitations.
